candidates.title: Restore access to a self-hosted workflow account

demandEvidence.chore: Concrete account-recovery request assessed as a checklist experiment
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How do I recover access to the original owner account / make my existing workflows visible again without losing them?

ease.reason: A sample checklist can organize a recovery request, but no supplied implementation reference supports account recovery or workflow restoration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent automation consultants might charge for guided recovery; this post proves neither a buyer nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can produce a checklist from synthetic details, while platform recovery and preserving workflows require authorized human action.

autonomy.reason: Only a person can verify ownership, use supported recovery paths and confirm workflows remain intact; unattended account changes are unsuitable.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly asks to recover owner access and retain workflow visibility, but gives no procedure or repeat frequency.

candidates.reason: Concrete account-recovery request assessed as a checklist experiment; below threshold because the task is sensitive, largely human-dependent, and lacks implementation support.

candidates.title: Draft status updates from changing order data

demandEvidence.chore: Concrete status-update chore assessed as a fictional-row draft experiment
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d be interested to hear how others handle customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.

ease.reason: A beginner can test draft wording against fictional order rows, but no supplied implementation reference supports data connections or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online shops may pay to prepare clearer order updates; the discussion establishes no purchase or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can turn operator-supplied status fields into draft messages, but live data mapping and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed tool could flag incomplete fields and draft an update, while staff must verify order facts and approve sending.

evidence.reason: The request identifies customer-facing status updates when operational data is incomplete or changes, but gives no frequency or detailed rules.

candidates.reason: Concrete status-update chore assessed as a fictional-row draft experiment; below threshold because no implementation evidence, detailed rules, or repeated volume is supplied.

candidates.title: Prepare a restaurant order alert

demandEvidence.chore: A concrete order-notification chore merits a narrow sample-order alert experiment
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A beginner can test one synthetic order and alert text, but no supplied reference documents the website trigger or WhatsApp delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small restaurant might pay to reduce missed order alerts; this request does not establish buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can draft or simulate alerts from operator-supplied sample orders; a live website and WhatsApp connection remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop could format a supplied order into an alert, but no source supports trigger or delivery and a person should verify it.

evidence.reason: The request states a desired order-notification system for a restaurant website, but not its frequency, inputs, setup or payment.

candidates.reason: A concrete order-notification chore merits a narrow sample-order alert experiment; below threshold because trigger and delivery capabilities lack supplied implementation evidence.
